history.notes: Two fixes: the 'Verify N transactions' prompt no longer counts your pays (incoming rows are confirmed on Today or kept as history, never 'to verify'), and the Coin Catcher starts on the first arrow press and takes the arrows from anywhere on the Score page — no need to click the play area first.

Today, rebuilt calm: four cards (Safe to Spend, This week vs your typical week, your four account balances, Homestead), the Do-this-now strip, the money-flow bar, and two closed sections — Daily Pulse & rewards, and Plan & upcoming — with everything else behind 'details'. New: 'Your accounts now' (enter what's in Everyday, Bills, Savings and Investment; Safe to Spend starts from Everyday; offered after your first statement, on the Accounts card and under More). 'Unknown' is a standard category for small amounts that fit nowhere.

Snappier and tidier: resizing the window and switching pages is now immediate (hidden pages no longer take part in layout, and two resize handlers that forced full layout passes are gone — a resize went from several seconds to a fraction of one). The welcome pack and the level celebration wait until the file picker is closed and the statement is sorted, so nothing opens over the folder window any more.

A clean first run: the welcome pack and Gerald's tour now wait until you've finished importing, sorting and confirming — nothing pops over the sort window any more. After your first statement, a 'Confirm what I found' step asks 'Is this your pay?' (amount, cadence and source read from the statement), offers the statement's closing balance as your Everyday balance, and lists the regular charges to confirm. The split editor has '+ New category…', sort cards show only real categories, suggested bills get clean names, and the first screen no longer asks for a pay figure.

Less to read: page subtitles, tips and hints are gone where the screen already says it, labels are single words (Name, Amount, Date, Already saved), the Statements page is Import statement / Sort / Commit / Clear with a plain 'Preview', and the Plan rows lost their 'click to edit' captions. Nothing was removed.

Follow-ups: confirming a suggested bill no longer completes the 'add money to a fund' challenge; suggested bills get clean names (Netflix, not Netflix Com); people tracking first no longer see a Setup warning badge or a 'Setup 0/7' count — the health line tracks statement, sorting, pays and learning instead; and when a pay lands with nothing in the plan to absorb it, a toast offers to put the learned savings amount aside in one click.

The app now learns how to split your pay: Today shows 'hold $X for bills · keep $Y for a normal fortnight · $Z to savings' from what you actually do (click to copy), how this week compares with your typical week and which category is running hot, and what's truly free after a normal rest of cycle. Analysis can set your target mix from your typical shares. Gerald answers 'what's my typical week' and 'is this a big week'. A reminder lands at six and ten weeks of data.

A new beginning: no plan needed. First run is two cards (how you're paid, bring in a statement). Today shows where your money goes — income to bills, categories and what's left — learns your typical week from your statements, spots regular charges and asks 'is this a bill?' with one click, and tells you how much of each pay is free to put aside. Analysis gains 'Typical week & big weeks'. The full money plan, set-asides and goals are still there, now optional.

Three small frictions fixed: every date field now takes '27/10', '15 Nov', '28th' and the like (not only full dates), including the Analysis custom range; the Plan header shows an Undo link for two minutes after you remove a row; and the Bills table's Priority and Frequency are one readable 'fortnightly · essential' column.

A quieter, more professional look: one hairline border on every card (no coloured outlines), no decorative accent bars, a flat slimmer top bar, a title-only navigation rail that fits a laptop screen, neutral badges, plain table rows and pills, and Plan rows with a tidy ⋯ menu for Edit and Remove. Nothing was removed.

Gerald now asks what you pay for: a bill interview (rent, power, phone, insurance, streaming, gym and more) one question at a time. Say yes and either type the amount, let your next statement fill it in, or flag it to come back to — pending bills show on Today, the Plan and the sort cards until they have an amount.

Money plan wizard: 'Your money right now' asks for the balance of each of your four accounts (Everyday, Bills, Savings, Investment) instead of one total. 'Suggest a split' uses those balances, and the transfer step now shows what each account has today and the exact moves to make.
Money plan wizard: the transfer step now lists all four accounts, with empty ones explained instead of hidden
Reimbursements: mark an expense 'getting reimbursed', see it on Today until the money comes back, and assign any incoming amount to it in full or in part — spending nets off automatically
Split one purchase across several categories: 'Split…' on the sort card, or right-click any transaction; Analysis, the pie, the month report and pacts count each part
Sort queue: the overview now scrolls and lists every merchant (click one to start there); cards scroll so 'Make it a recurring bill' shows its fields on smaller screens

Calmer Today: the Pulse collapses to a strip once done, pacts and the monthly event fold into one section, a single quick-action row with a More menu, systems reveal themselves as you go (Settings can show everything), fewer stacked toasts and celebrations
